summary.headline: Bajaj Electricals Q1 FY27: revenue up 2.3% YoY while EBIT margin rose to 6.6% from 2.5%, led by consumer products margin recovery to 3.9%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 2.3% YoY in Q1 FY27, with consumer products up 1.7% (after multiple quarters of decline) and lighting solutions up 4.4%. Consolidated EBIT margin expanded to 6.6% from 2.5%, with consumer products EBIT margin at 3.9% versus negative 1.7% a year earlier, driven by gross margin gains and operating leverage. Fans remained the weak spot, with management attributing share loss to operational issues including gas and PCB shortages. Management guided to 8-10% growth on a blended basis (described as a non-binding aspiration) and a 6-7% margin stabilisation for the next two years before a move toward 10% in consumer products. Cash flow from operations was negative in the quarter, mainly due to tax payments linked to the Morphy Richards acquisition.

financial_highlights.change: consumer products gross margin up 220 bps
debtors improved, inventory slightly up seasonally
due to tax and TDS/GST payments on Morphy Richards acquisition; ex these, described as healthy

segments.name: Consumer products
segments.commentary: Revenue +1.7% YoY with a split: cooling (fans, coolers) contracted while non-summer categories grew double digits; Morphy Richards grew double digits post acquisition. EBIT margin 3.9% vs -1.7% a year ago. Fans lost share; management plans to claw back in two to three quarters.

segments.name: Lighting solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue +4.4% YoY, with double-digit growth in consumer lighting. EBIT margin about 7% as legacy professional lighting contracts signed before commodity inflation limited pass-through; management expects a return to double-digit margin after exiting these over a quarter or two.

guidance_outlook: Blended company growth of 8-10% per year targeted (management said this is not a forward-looking commitment); industry assumed to grow 6-7%.
Consumer products EBIT margin expected to stabilise at 6-7% over the next two years, with a longer-term target of about 10%; management said it would not come in the next two years.
Lighting EBIT margin expected to return to double digits once legacy professional lighting contracts roll off.
No major price increases expected for the rest of FY27 at this stage, but management said this could change within two months given volatility.
Fan share expected to be recovered over the next two to three quarters.
capex_capacity: Wires entry progressing better than expected; management did not disclose current-quarter contribution. Wires sit within lighting and switchgears.
Management is evaluating adjacent opportunities including solar, cables, and professional lighting; no timelines given, described as early stage.
BLDC fans: industry BLDC penetration estimated at 30-35%; Bajaj is slightly under-indexed but growing faster.
demand_pricing: Cost inflation across categories ranged from about 6% to 11-12%, with coolers as high as 13%. Part was recovered through selective price increases and part through savings.

Fan volumes declined due to supply constraints (gas shortage during the war period and PCB shortages as BLDC demand exceeded plans), plus operational issues; gas supply restored, PCB supply being covered on longer cycles.
Overall market share mixed: stable in most categories, gaining in iron and mixer grinders, losing in fans.
E-commerce about 15-20% of consumer business, growing double digits; quick commerce 8-10% of e-commerce. Alternate channels about 45% of business, modern/general split about 55:45.
Exports almost doubled. Weak in South, strongest in East (per management).
Competition increasing as new players enter; management expects the market to expand as a result.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fans lag, and what are the BLDC and premiumisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Vishal Chadha said fans declined, and price increases kept pace with commodity inflation. BLDC is estimated at 30-35% of industry, with Bajaj slightly under-indexed but growing faster.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly can lighting margins return toward double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Sachdeva said legacy professional lighting contracts signed before the war limited price pass-through, a temporary blip. Margins should recover within a quarter or two as these exit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consumer products margin path and timeline to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Sachdeva said margins should stabilise at 6-7% for the next two years, with a steady path toward 10% thereafter, timing dependent on brand investment and scale.

qa_highlights.question: Market share trend and rural performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Share stable or growing in most categories except fans, which is losing share; management has no separate rural share data but assumes rural share is intact.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors improved, inventory slightly up for the season; working capital days in the 50-60 range. Operating cash flow negative due to Morphy Richards-related tax and TDS/GST payments.

qa_highlights.question: Cost inflation and pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost inflation of 6-11% (coolers up to 13%), partly recovered through pricing and partly through savings. No major price increases seen as needed for the rest of the year, subject to commodity movement.

risks_watch: Fan recovery: whether share loss reverses within two to three quarters, given PCB and supply constraints.
Commodity inflation and the possibility of further price actions, which management says could change within two months.
Lighting margin recovery depends on exit timing of legacy professional lighting contracts.
Working capital and operating cash flow normalisation after Morphy Richards-related payments.
Competitive intensity increasing with new entrants, especially in consumer categories.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margin recovery and the consumer products turnaround, though guarded on forward growth and pricing, which management repeatedly qualified as volatile. Evasive on specifics for wires contribution and on distribution-level detail.
key_quotes: We delivered overall revenue growth of 2.3%. However, our EBIT margin improved to 6.6% from 2.5%.
But this is not a forward-looking commitment. But this is the kind of targets which we are looking at.

growth.why: Management guided 8-10% blended growth over two years (explicitly described as a non-binding aspiration, assuming industry growth of 6-7%), while Q1 revenue grew only 2.3%; backing rests on fan share recovery in 2-3 quarters, margin recovery and the Wires entry, with no specific capacity, orders or timelines quantified.
